warnings: This paper does NOT measure grain Zn concentration - it measures yield components, protein content, but no Zn biofortification data
Study focuses on Zn effects under salinity stress, not Zn biofortification for human nutrition
Multiple Zn rates used (0, 20, 40 kg/ha field; 0, 0.4, 0.8 g/pot greenhouse) but no grain Zn concentration reported
Factorial design with K×Zn interactions - treatments are combinations, not simple Zn vs control
Two separate experiments (greenhouse and field) with different units and application rates
Duncan's Multiple Range test used for mean separation, not standard error/LSD reporting

WARNING: LETTER-VAR - Variance shown as letters (a,b,c), not numbers

recon.variance_source: Duncan's new multiple range (DMR) test was used to compare the treatment means... Means followed by the same letter do not differ significantly at p 50.05by Duncan's new multiple range tests
recon.control_definition: Zn0 = 0 kg Zn ha⁻¹ in field, Zn0 = 0 g Zn pot⁻¹ in greenhouse
recon.treatment_definition: Zn1 = 20 kg ha⁻¹ field/0.4 g pot⁻¹ greenhouse; Zn2 = 40 kg ha⁻¹ field/0.8 g pot⁻¹ greenhouse, as ZnSO4
recon.potential_tc_confusion: Factorial design means control is Zn0K0, but treatments include Zn0K1, Zn0K2, etc. - only Zn effect comparisons are valid for meta-analysis
recon.sample_size_source: randomized complete block design with three replications was employed
recon.extraction_guidance: This paper should be EXCLUDED from the Zn biofortification meta-analysis as it does not measure grain Zn concentration. It focuses on agronomic performance under salinity stress, not nutritional biofortification. The outcome variables are yield components and protein content, not mineral concentrations.
